definition: One of the earliest and simplest types of artificial neural network, consisting of a single layer that makes binary classification decisions based on a weighted sum of inputs.
details: The perceptron, though limited to linearly separable problems, was a foundational concept in the history of neural networks and directly inspired the development of more complex multi-layer architectures.

explainer.lead: The perceptron is one of the earliest and simplest neural networks: a single layer that makes binary decisions from a weighted sum of inputs. Though limited to linearly separable problems, it was foundational to neural network history and inspired deeper architectures.

tiers.eli5: It adds up its inputs, each multiplied by a weight, and if the total crosses a threshold it says yes, otherwise no.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers treat the single-layer perceptron as a binary classifier based on a weighted sum of inputs, and its known ceiling is that it only handles linearly separable problems, which is why multi-layer architectures followed.
tiers.paperLevel: A single-layer artificial neural network that makes binary classification decisions from a weighted sum of inputs; it is limited to linearly separable problems and directly inspired more complex multi-layer architectures.

explainer.example: A perceptron weighing several input features, summing them and thresholding the total, decides whether an item belongs to class A or class B.

citation.title: The Perceptron: A Probabilistic Model for Information Storage and Organization in the Brain
